title: Ten real web pages: 91% fewer tokens

plain.say: On ten real web pages, the readable text came to 91% fewer tokens than the page's markup (583,220 tokens down to 49,899).
plain.holdsWhen: The ten pages were fetched live on 28 Oct 2026 and counted with a proxy tokenizer (o200k_base). They are modern, script-heavy pages, and the saving ranged from 71% to 99%.
plain.doesntTell: Older, plainer HTML will save less. A proxy tokenizer is not Claude's, so read the figure as indicative. Ten pages is a small sample, so this is not a general saving.

needles: The pages are modern and script-heavy

command:
python3 scripts/benchmark/pages.py fetch DIR
EVAL_IN=DIR EVAL_OUT=OUT npx vitest run tests/extraction-dump.test.ts
python3 scripts/benchmark/pages.py measure DIR OUT

title: Plain text and code: no saving

plain.say: Leaving out the one HTML page, the readable notes for the text, Markdown, code, JSON and CSV files came to 23,073 tokens against 22,344 for the originals, which is 3% more.
plain.holdsWhen: A 15-file corpus built from the repository's own files and prose, measured on 27 Oct 2026 with a proxy tokenizer.
plain.doesntTell: It saves tokens only where a file carries markup. On text and code the value is orientation and readability, not compression, and the handoff note itself adds 255 tokens. The corpus is small.

needles: does not make text smaller, and it does not claim to

command:
npm run dev   # in one terminal
python3 scripts/benchmark/make_corpus.py DIR
python3 scripts/benchmark/measure.py DIR RESULTS.json http://127.0.0.1:8787

title: Office files: readable text instead of XML

plain.say: Three Office files that an agent cannot read directly came out as 2,635 tokens of readable text, against 10,090 tokens of the XML inside them.
plain.holdsWhen: A DOCX, an XLSX and a PPTX built for the test from the repository's own prose, measured on 27 Oct 2026.
plain.doesntTell: The files are synthetic, so real Word, Excel and PowerPoint files will behave differently.

needles: The containers are synthetic, so real-world Office and PDF files will behave differently

command:
python3 scripts/benchmark/make_corpus.py DIR
python3 scripts/benchmark/measure.py DIR RESULTS.json http://127.0.0.1:8787

title: PDFs: 99.3% of a reference extractor's words

plain.say: Across 59 PDFs, the reader found 99.3% of the words that poppler's pdftotext found, weighted by word count. The median file scored 100%.
plain.holdsWhen: PDFs from Chrome, macOS, Ghostscript and TeX, ReportLab, and others. Recall is the share of the reference's words that appear in the output.
plain.doesntTell: Three of the 59 scored under 90%: two Japanese and Korean files with no character map, and one where a font maps a ligature to the digit 1. Files from Word, LibreOffice, InDesign and Google Docs were not tested, and reading order for columns was not measured.

needles: files from Microsoft Word, LibreOffice, InDesign, and Google Docs were not available to test
reading order for multi-column pages was not measured

command:
EVAL_IN=DIR EVAL_OUT=OUT npx vitest run tests/extraction-dump.test.ts
python3 scripts/benchmark/compare_extraction.py DIR OUT

title: EPUB books: median 100% of pandoc's words

plain.say: On 27 books, the reader found a median of 100% of the words that pandoc found, and 98.0% weighted by word count.
plain.holdsWhen: Project Gutenberg, Standard Ebooks and IDPF sample books, including a Japanese book and an Arabic one, and a Wikisource book, compared with pandoc -f epub -t plain.
plain.doesntTell: One book, a linear algebra textbook, scored 80%, because pandoc writes equations as TeX commands and this reader writes the symbols. A book made only of pictures is refused with a reason.

needles: pandoc writes equations as TeX commands
A book made only of pictures is refused with a reason

command:
EVAL_IN=DIR EVAL_OUT=OUT npx vitest run tests/extraction-dump.test.ts
python3 scripts/benchmark/compare_extraction.py DIR OUT

title: Web pages: median 99.9% of pandoc's words

plain.say: On the same ten web pages, the reader found a median of 99.9% of the words that pandoc found, or 96.7% weighted by word count.
plain.holdsWhen: Word recall against pandoc -f html -t plain on ten live pages, taken on 28 Oct 2026.
plain.doesntTell: The recipe page scored 56%, because pandoc also reads text the page hides, such as menus and consent notices, that this reader leaves out on purpose. A page that needs scripts to show its content comes out nearly empty, and the reader says so.

needles: pandoc also reads text the page hides (menus, consent notices) that this reader leaves out on purpose
pages that need scripts to show their content
